name: BookingKoala
tagline: All-in-one booking, scheduling, dispatch and payments software aimed at home service businesses like cleaning companies.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: The part everyone actually thinks about, a public booking form with service options, pricing rules, availability and a calendar of jobs, is a solid one-session build. The part nobody thinks about is everything after the booking: recurring schedules that survive reschedules, assigning providers without double-booking them, provider pay calculations, automated reminder texts, tip and card-on-file handling, and a phone-friendly view for the person actually holding a mop. An agent will get you a working single-operator booking system in a weekend, and it will be genuinely fine if you are one or two people. The moment you have a dozen providers, franchise locations, or a payroll run that has to be right, you are rebuilding a company's product with a spreadsheet's error handling. Payments and SMS also mean real third-party accounts, so this never gets to be purely local.
coreLoopDIY: A public booking form with service pricing rules and availability, writing jobs into a database, plus an admin calendar to assign, reschedule and mark jobs complete.
requirements: A server or host that stays up, because customers book on it
Stripe account if you want deposits or card-on-file
Twilio or similar if you want SMS reminders, otherwise email only
Somebody willing to be on-call when the booking form breaks on a Saturday
whatYouLose: Provider-facing mobile experience and job notifications
Provider pay, tips and payroll reporting
Automated reminder, follow-up and review-request sequences
Recurring booking logic that handles skips, reschedules and price changes without corrupting the series
Multi-location and franchise separation, plus the reporting that comes with it
moatNotes: The lock-in is operational, not technical: once your customers, recurring schedules and provider pay rates live in it, migrating is a live-business surgery, not an export.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because a service business owner is not shipping software, they are dispatching crews, and every hour spent debugging their own booking form is an hour not spent selling jobs. The software is boring and mostly solved, and the price is small next to one missed recurring client. The value is not clever code, it is that the reminder texts fire, the provider app shows today's route, and the pay report is defensible at the end of the month.
notes: Fine DIY target if you are a solo operator; a bad DIY target the day you have employees who get paid from it.
prompt:
Build a self-hosted booking and job scheduling app for a small home-service business (think house cleaning) that I will run for myself.

Stack, no substitutions:
- Next.js (App Router) with TypeScript and Tailwind
- SQLite via Prisma, file at ./data/app.db
- Single admin login using a password hash in .env, cookie session, no user accounts for customers
- No telemetry, no analytics, no third-party SDKs beyond what is listed below

Public side:
- A booking page at / with a multi-step form: service type, bedrooms/bathrooms or a generic quantity field, extras (checkboxes with prices), frequency (one-time, weekly, biweekly, monthly), date and time slot, address, contact info
- Live price calculation from configurable rules stored in the DB: base price per service, per-unit price, extras, frequency discount percentage, tax percentage
- Availability comes from configurable weekly working hours plus a max-jobs-per-slot number; show only slots that are open
- On submit, create the booking (and, for recurring, generate the next 12 occurrences), send a plain confirmation email

Admin side at /admin:
- Week and day calendar of jobs with status (scheduled, in progress, done, cancelled)
- Create, reschedule, cancel a single occurrence or the whole recurring series (ask which)
- Assign a provider from a simple providers table; block assigning a provider to overlapping jobs
- A mobile-friendly /today view listing a provider's jobs with address, notes and a done button
- Customer list with job history and lifetime revenue
- Settings screens for services, extras, pricing rules and working hours

Explicitly in scope: seed script with one service and sample bookings, email via SMTP creds in .env (log to console if unset), a README with setup steps.
Explicitly out of scope: payments, SMS, payroll, multi-location, reviews, marketing automation, provider native apps. Leave a clearly marked TODO where Stripe would plug in.

All secrets in .env with a .env.example. Do not add a cloud database or any hosted service. Make it run with npm install, npx prisma migrate dev, npm run dev.
